source: TL2 summaries of public reporting; each item links to its source.

items.headline: Anthropic says the junior share of its technical hires fell to 9%
items.line: Anthropic says the junior share of its technical hires fell from 27% to 9%, and that by August its employees' interactive AI agent hours outnumbered their own working hours six to one.

items.headline: AICPA issues a practice aid on AI in financial statement audits
items.line: The Journal of Accountancy reports the AICPA issued a practice aid on how a company's use of AI in financial reporting, and an audit firm's own use of AI, affect a financial statement audit, and the AICPA's chief auditor said the auditor remains responsible for the audit and the opinion.

items.headline: AICPA and AIUC pair a SOC 2 report with an AI agent certification
items.line: The Journal of Accountancy reports the AICPA and the Artificial Intelligence Underwriting Company launched a single CPA-led engagement that combines a SOC 2 report with AIUC-1 certification for AI systems and agents.

items.headline: Federal agencies issue voluntary security guidance for testing frontier AI
items.line: CyberScoop reports that CISA, the NSA and a Commerce Department standards center issued voluntary joint guidance urging AI companies to use technical controls, independent testing and shutdown policies when they test frontier models in sandbox environments.

items.headline: Meta releases the weights for its Muse Spark Open model
items.line: Meta says Muse Spark Open, a model with 816 billion total parameters and a 1 million-token context window, is available through several API platforms, with its weights downloadable from Hugging Face and the major cloud providers.

items.headline: White House names its intelligence chief to lead its new AI task force
items.line: NPR reports President Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to lead a new "Super Intelligence Force" that will coordinate the federal government's work with AI companies and other groups.

items.headline: Gemini 4 Argon's opening price doubles after launch
items.line: Google says Argon starts at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, rising to $4 and $20 after an introductory period; early access is limited to cyber defenders and trusted testers.

items.headline: Report: Oracle signs a $7 billion, five-year compute deal with Tencent
items.line: Citing the Financial Times, The Next Web says the roughly 100,000 chips sit in Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia, with about 30% paid upfront; the report is unconfirmed.
